items.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Mr. Magic – not only Mr. Magic, but the one before that that was a hit, it was not – he was not designed to be the leader on the date.

ctx.x: Please tell us. Tell the world.

Man. Mr. Magic – not only Mr. Magic, but the one before that that was a hit, it was not – he was not designed to be the leader on the date. What happened was, they had the rhythm section all poised to record at Rudy’s, and as it turned out, it was either Hank Crawford or Stanley Turrentine who didn’t show up. So they were waiting around the studio, waiting, waiting. Nobody showed up. So Creed just – I don’t even think he had a tenor saxophone. He had just alto. So they had to go get a saxophone for him to play,…

What’s the name of that tune that – God. That first – Grover had a hit before Mr. Magic. It was something else. I can’t recall what it was. But, like I said, the rhythm section was – he was just pulled out of the guys who were supposed to be the background players, the sidemen. That’s how he ended up having his successful career.
